Unit count (36) is ~25% above target due to oauth.rs's 20 tests covering 6 round-1 attack vectors with branched negative paths.

The fixed-algorithm validation IS the defense; gap is test surface only.

T5's pending_user_cap.rs guards this at the per-jwt-sub level rather than per-IP. Acceptable architectural choice.
per_area_findings.audit_severity: MINOR — both gaps are documented and acceptable for hackathon; route-level limiter exists, downstream layer covers per-user cap.

criterion_check.uses_tokio_time_pause_advance: DEVIATION — line 151 uses tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1100)) wall-clock against a 1s TTL store. T8 decisions log line 424 flagged this explicitly: PendingBundles reads chrono::Utc::now() which tokio's instrumented clock cannot influence. tech-spec line 227 prescribed tokio::time::pause+advance; it would not work against wall-clock without refactoring PendingBundles to tokio::time::Instant.

criterion_check.50_successful_then_51st_429: DEVIATION — accepts EITHER HTTP 429 OR HTTP 200 with JSON-RPC error envelope mentioning 'per-user pending bundle cap' (line 124-131). summary: All 13 focus areas pass the audit, with 7 minor deviations explicitly documented in T1-T9 decisions.md and acceptable for a size-L hackathon MVP. Test pyramid is healthy (36 unit + 7 wasm + 22 integration + 3 webapp + 10 manual smoke steps), slightly above the size-L target but each test is single-purpose and traceable to a user-spec MUST or Decision-9/10/11/12 invariant. Critical recall ownership isolation passes with explicit cross-tenant assertion. No deploy-blocking gaps. Test Audit verdict: PASS_WITH_NOTES.
